purpose: Open, game-need-first map of factual premises for military reality in a thirteenth-century Novgorod RPG. It is a static research and sampling aid, not a corpus inventory, a scenario roster, a combat ruleset, or proof that a military event is present.
guardrails: The named situations are probes, not a whitelist of military actions or scenes.
A claim supports only its stated qualitative premise; current people, arms, supplies, orders, routes, injuries, ownership and outcomes remain committed-world state.
Exact damage, hit resolution, body state, movement, inventory, permissions, time, persistence and combat consequences stay with their existing code owners.
This pass is static only: it does not run live gameplay, repair gameplay owners, or claim gameplay saturation.

factual_families.scope: People in armed, supporting, civic-defence and noncombatant roles; authority, dependency and the difference between a named record and a general institution.
factual_needs: What roles can be distinguished without assuming a standing modern army: commander, retainer, militia participant, messenger, scout, craft worker, carrier, healer, guard and civilian?
What social status, obligation, local authority and household ties can shape participation, access to equipment and treatment of others?
residual_needs: Broader source-backed role and status map for Novgorod and its hinterland
Bounded treatment of obligations and civilian participation
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No current roster, command authority, loyalty, knowledge, permission or decision is inferred.

factual_families.scope: Historically compatible weapon, armour and carrying categories; fitting, use limits, wear, storage, damage, maintenance and repair as factual premises.
factual_needs: What weapon, protection, clothing, belt, harness and carried-tool classes are compatible with the setting?
How do moisture, corrosion, edge condition, fastening, leather, wood and ordinary handling constrain serviceability without inventing exact combat values?
residual_needs: Weapon and armour form/use/repair families beyond isolated finds
Shield, bowstring, arrow, spear, scabbard and fastening premises
Period-compatible carrying and field-maintenance practices
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No object, ownership, condition, protection value, reach, ammunition, damage or successful repair is created.

factual_families.scope: Practice, conditioning, handling familiarity, rest, exertion, thirst, cold and ordinary readiness limits.
factual_needs: What distinguishes drilled practice, novice handling and experienced routine without assigning skill to a particular person?
How do carrying, repetitive friction, cold, sleep loss, food and fluid needs constrain sustained activity?
residual_needs: Qualitative training and readiness premises
Sleep, load-carrying and group-rest relations
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No skill level, fatigue value, stamina, schedule or performance outcome follows.

factual_families.scope: How groups maintain contact, visibility, hearing, orders, handover, assembly and confusion in changing terrain and weather.
factual_needs: What makes voice, visual and messenger signals more or less usable?
How can density, line of sight, noise and local leadership affect coordination without asserting a fixed doctrine?
residual_needs: Period-compatible signalling and command practice
Formation and cohesion under changing ground and visibility
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No order, allegiance, doctrine, morale, perception or group decision is supplied.

factual_families.scope: Movement, halts, camp routines, observation, concealment, traces, scouting and ambush conditions.
factual_needs: What do ground, weather, daylight, sound, smoke, animals and traffic traces make easier or harder to notice and traverse?
What shelter, water, fuel, sanitation, guarding and resupply questions arise in a temporary camp?
residual_needs: Camp selection, scouting, concealment and trace-reading families
Field sanitation and temporary-shelter premises
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No route, enemy presence, camp, hidden person, detection result or safe passage is inferred.

factual_families.scope: Qualitative differences among mounted, foot and ranged participants, including animal handling and terrain dependence.
factual_needs: How do horse behaviour, harness, footing, forage, water, weather and threat response constrain mounted movement?
What material and environmental premises affect carrying, foot movement and projectile use without calculating a strike?
residual_needs: Mounted and foot formation/use constraints
Ranged-weapon handling, ammunition and weather premises
Horse care under campaign conditions
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No horse, rider, harness, ammunition, control, speed, target or combat result is created.

factual_families.scope: Food, water, fodder, fuel, carts, sledges, boats, loads, river crossings and their practical limits.
factual_needs: How do storage, spoilage, animal feed, weather, ground and load affect supply continuity?
What do water level, current, ice, landing edges, bridges, boats and temporary means imply qualitatively for movement and delay?
residual_needs: Campaign provisioning and fodder families
Crossing, bridge, ford and boat-use premises

factual_families.scope: Approaches, walls, gates, timber-earth structures, observation, fire, smoke, repair, evacuation and containment.
factual_needs: What is historically compatible about timber-and-earth defensive construction and its exposure to water, soil and fire?
What qualitative effects can smoke, visibility, crowding, tools, water and local repair needs have without assuming a specific siege machine or plan?
residual_needs: Thirteenth-century Novgorod defence and siege material culture
Fire spread, emergency movement and ordinary repair context
Gate, wall, ditch and civic-defence operational families

factual_families.scope: Ground, slope, vegetation, water, mud, snow, ice, wind, rain, fog, temperature, smoke and natural light as military environment.
factual_needs: How do season and weather alter footing, sight, sound, wetness, cold, fire, smoke and work?
How do forest, field, bank, wetland, settlement and water edge create differing practical constraints?

factual_families.scope: Injury mechanisms, observable red flags, immediate bounded aid, carrying, rest and the limits of diagnosis and treatment.
factual_needs: What physical injury, bleeding, burn, cold-exposure, fracture and infection premises help distinguish a reasonable attempt from a guaranteed outcome?
What makes immediate care, moving a person, stopping work and seeking qualified help relevant without importing a modern medical system into 1230?
residual_needs: Historical care roles and constraints
Transport/evacuation and disability premises
Broader wound, infection and recovery composition
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No injury, diagnosis, treatment resource, severity, survival, recovery, evacuation or body-state transition is decided here.

factual_families.scope: Practical, legal, social and material premises around surrender, restraint, escape, pursuit, property, confiscation, captives and returns.
factual_needs: What constraints of terrain, fatigue, visibility, social control and transport shape capture, escape and pursuit?
What historical and ordinary distinctions are needed before discussing taken goods, prisoners, compensation or return to civilian life?
residual_needs: Period-compatible captivity, ransom, spoils, restraint and return context
Flight/pursuit practical premises across terrain and weather
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No crime, title transfer, captivity, authority, prisoner, pursuit result or entitlement is inferred.

factual_families.scope: Effects on households, dwellings, food, animals, water, waste, fire, displacement, repair, work, fear and social recovery.
factual_needs: What ordinary household and environmental needs become salient after disruption without assuming that violence occurred?
How do damaged shelter, contaminated food or water, lost labour, displaced animals, smoke and repair work interact qualitatively?
residual_needs: Displacement, damaged-housing, livestock-loss and civilian recovery families
Civilian social and legal aftermath without treating an episode as a universal rule
factual_families.code_owner_boundary: No destruction, displaced person, loss, contamination, repair, claim, ownership or recovery outcome is created.

sampling_policy.stratified_rule: The 75 cases draw from rotating factual families and cross-cutting axes; they are not a fixed per-family quota or a permanent examination.
sampling_policy.free_rule: The 25 cases have no supplied primary domain. Their generator may combine unusual places, people, activities, weather, time, maintenance and civilian consequences to expose omissions outside the current map.
sampling_policy.independence: Blind situation generators receive no WK answers. Separate WK-only readers receive frozen inputs and reconstruct only from WK. A significant unsupported premise is a knowledge gap; generators and readers must not repair it with invented mechanics or current-world facts.
lifecycle: Record substantial unsupported premises as gaps
Add and independently review static factual claims
Replay only known gaps against the updated corpus

not_a_completeness_verdict: This open map guides continuing static expansion. Coverage of a batch cannot prove complete military reality or gameplay saturation.
